judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses correctly identified and fixed the Include/Update duplication, cross-product batching, and overly-broad clean issues. judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses correctly diagnose all three problems with strong, accurate explanations. They are largely equivalent on the first three criteria. Response A edges ahead by correctly noting that FileWrites must be declared at evaluation time (since dotnet clean doesn't run the generation target first), whereas Response B recommends registering FileWrites inside the target, which is less correct for clean tracking. A also provides more complete concrete code.

Both responses used essentially the identical approach (Compile Update/Remove, paired data-schema batching, IntermediateOutputPath, FileWrites registration), hit the same intermediate semicolon-escaping bug, recovered the same way, and verified all four requirements with successful build (0 warnings), 2 validation runs, intermediate-only generation, and clean removal. Response A additionally verified source-preservation, but this is a minor difference. Outcomes are equivalent.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Build multiple configurations with unique binlogs
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A located the project, built both Debug and Release with unique binlogs, and succeeded. Response B falsely claimed the directory was not a project root and refused, without even running ls—yet the project files were present. A fully accomplished the task; B failed entirely.

Both built successfully and created a binlog, but B followed the best practice of using /bl:{} for a unique auto-generated filename, while A hardcoded msbuild.binlog which overwrites on every build. B also verified the binlog exists. B is clearly better on the rubric criteria."

Both responses produced a valid binlog and avoided bare -bl. However, the key rubric criterion specifically requires the properly PowerShell-escaped `-bl:{{}}` form, which only B used. A used a fixed filename and its command actually errored on the ErrorActionPreference assignment due to quoting issues. B also methodically explored the project structure and verified the binlog's existence. B satisfies all three criteria cleanly; A fails the first one.
